international.title: Timms says Pip review being published today will ‘rehumanise’ benefit – UK politics live
international.summary: Some recommendations expected to clash with those of Milburn’s recent report into Neets UK disability benefit cuts ‘risk worsening youth destitution’ Andy Burnham has announced an ambition to get a million more girls involved in sport by the time the UK hosts the Women’s World Cup in 2035 . The Press Association reports: Sporting organisations will be required to demonstrate “structural equality” to receive public funding as part of the drive, the government said. Officials said the ambition would take into account how women and girls show up in viewing figures, coaching positions and on boards, as well as seeking to ensure they have the same access as boys to sports like football and rugby in school. When the review is published, the review will call for a fundamental overhaul to rehumanise Pip … There are a number of difficulties with the current system. Pip is a highly valued benefit but the current assessment is not fit for purpose, and tomorrow we will set out proposals to change it. We will set out the view that in addition to a cash benefit from Pip, which we are recommending should remain a cash-first benefit, there may well be services that would be helpful to people as part of their Pip award. The Motability scheme already enables many disabled people to enjoy the mobility that they would not otherwise be able to enjoy, and they choose to forgo part of their cash benefit in return for access to the scheme. We think that principle could be applied more widely with the Pip scheme. Continue reading...
